title: Jurassic Park Arcade
headline: A gun that pushes back while you tranquilize an island.
intro: Jurassic Park Arcade (Raw Thrills, 2015) swaps a handheld rifle for a mounted gun the player physically pushes against mechanical resistance to aim, tracking real dinosaurs across nine short missions. There is no reload and no running out of primary ammo — Raw Thrills' own operator manual and two independent player accounts agree the trigger fires an unlimited tranquilizer stream, while a separate thumb button throws a strictly limited supply of grenades. Three boss dinosaurs — Triceratops, Tyrannosaurus, and Spinosaurus — anchor the story, and shooting a stranded human colleague by mistake costs health, not points.

referenceScope.reason: Raw Thrills' own 2023 operator's manual, two independent player reviews, and the manufacturer's gun-assembly parts drawings together document this release's control hardware, gameplay loop, and penalties more completely than any other Jurassic Park arcade title.
referenceScope.caveat: Sega's 1994 System 32 and 1997 Model 3 titles use different control hardware and are referenced only to distinguish them, never as substitutes; cabinet-variant differences are in Release Notes. No cabinet has been selected for the build, and no game has been run, emulated, or measured here.

session.format: Nine short missions — three story arcs of three levels each — playable solo or two-player, each with an independently aimed and fired gun.
session.social: Two players share one screen but aim independently. A 2015 review describes choosing levels without first completing earlier ones, making shorter shared sessions possible.
session.failureToAvoid: An uncalibrated gun or confusing continue boundary breaks the shared run. One reviewer's complete playthrough took about 36 minutes and 10 continues; that is an example, not a minimum cost or promised session length.

playLoop.title: Choose a mission and join
playLoop.action: Choose a level and join solo or with a second player. Operator calibration belongs before guest play, not in the player's round.
playLoop.feedback: Nine levels are grouped into three story arcs; the 2015 review describes level selection without a prior full clear.
playLoop.skill: Choose a short episode or a longer run to suit the group.

playLoop.title: Push to aim
playLoop.action: Grip the mounted gun and pivot it within its travel range to track targets through an automatically advancing scene.
playLoop.feedback: The reticle follows two-axis position; the manual documents one potentiometer per axis. Motion resistance and response still require real-hardware validation.
playLoop.skill: Track a moving threat with a mounted mechanism rather than a handheld pointing device.

playLoop.title: Fire
playLoop.action: Pull the trigger to fire the primary tranquilizer weapon.
playLoop.feedback: Unlimited ammo — a Wilcox Arcade review and a Many Strange Things review each independently confirm no reload action exists in this game.
playLoop.skill: Track and prioritize threats without a primary-ammunition reload cycle; collected special weapons and grenades add separate resource decisions.

playLoop.title: Throw a grenade
playLoop.action: Press the grip's large thumb button, separate from the trigger, to throw one collected grenade.
playLoop.feedback: A limited-supply action, confirmed by two player reviews and Raw Thrills' own grip-assembly parts drawing: a Trigger and a Large Thumb Button, not a pump.
playLoop.skill: Saving grenades for a swarm moment or a boss opening, since supply is finite.

playLoop.title: Clear or continue
playLoop.action: Progress through the three-level story arcs toward Triceratops, Tyrannosaurus and Spinosaurus encounters, or continue after losing health.
playLoop.feedback: The reviews describe hidden ambrosia collectibles and special weapons as reasons to replay, alongside the large scripted encounters.
playLoop.skill: Replay for better execution and missed discoveries, not just to reach the ending.

screenRead.label: On-screen mission prompts
screenRead.meaning: Short text/icon cues tell the player when and where to shoot an incoming threat; a Wilcox Arcade review calls the difficulty 'incredibly fair' because of this prompting.

screenRead.label: Colleague / NPC hit feedback
screenRead.meaning: Shooting a stranded colleague by mistake costs the player health rather than scoring a hit — the opposite of shooting a dinosaur.

screenRead.label: Grenade / special-weapon count
screenRead.meaning: Tracks the limited supply of thrown grenades and any temporary hidden weapon pickup (e.g. the X-22 Renegade or Frostbite Cannon), both finite resources.

screenRead.label: Ambrosia collectible pickup
screenRead.meaning: A hidden per-level bonus item that adds score without affecting the mission outcome — a reason to look around, not just at threats.

signatureMoments.title: The Triceratops charge
signatureMoments.description: A Triceratops confronts the player's vehicle — a central encounter featured in Raw Thrills' pre-release promotional imagery. The gallery labels that image as a render, not live HUD capture.

signatureMoments.title: The Tyrannosaurus encounter
signatureMoments.description: The promotional gallery shows two large predators closing in. The 2015 review describes the second story arc's antagonist as the T-Rex, making scale and threat tracking part of the spectacle.

signatureMoments.title: The seat that stomps (Motion DLX only)
signatureMoments.description: On the Motion DLX cabinet, a reviewer describes the seat slamming hard enough to feel 'like a gigantic dinosaur stomping' beside the player — a motion-cabinet-specific effect, absent on the Environmental SD cabinet this page otherwise references.

controls.input: Mounted two-handled grip, pushed/pulled on a gimbal
controls.action: True two-axis position aim — not a relative-motion, mouse-style gun — read from a potentiometer on each axis per the manufacturer's own drawings.
controls.feel: Rubber/nylon 'stop bumpers' limit travel on both axes, but no dedicated return spring is documented at the pivot; whether the gun recentres on its own or must be pushed back is not established here and needs checking against real hardware.

controls.action: Fires the primary tranquilizer weapon with unlimited ammo and no reload action.
controls.feel: A single, always-available input — no pump, no magazine — confirmed by the parts list (Trigger plus Large Thumb Button only) and by two independent player accounts.

controls.input: Large thumb button (on the grip, away from the trigger)
controls.action: Throws a grenade from the player's limited supply.
controls.feel: A second, distinct input — do not copy the Big Buck Hunter station's pump-action design onto this one; this is a button, not a sliding mechanism.

controls.action: Provides physical gun feedback; the manual documents a shaker assembly and separately fused player solenoid power.
controls.feel: The feedback timing and force must be checked on real hardware. A parts list alone does not establish that every hit, shot or impact produces a particular effect.

buildPriorities.title: True positional aim, not a relative-motion gun
buildPriorities.why: The manual documents two potentiometers measuring the mounted gun's position. A handheld optical gun may also report absolute aim, but changes the support, travel and physical experience; it is not a mechanically equivalent swap.
buildPriorities.proof: A calibration check confirms the reticle matches the gun's true physical angle at both mechanical end-stops, not only at screen center.

buildPriorities.title: Don't invent a return spring or a pump
buildPriorities.why: No return spring is documented at the gimbal pivot, and the only secondary input is a thumb button, not a pump; a Big Buck Hunter-style reload motion here would misrepresent the real game.
buildPriorities.proof: The finished mount's at-rest behavior and its one secondary button are checked against this exact confirmed hardware before any panel is fabricated.

buildPriorities.title: Match the mechanical travel stops, not an arbitrary range
buildPriorities.why: The gimbal's 'stop bumper' parts hard-limit swing on each axis; an under- or over-built range changes the reticle-to-edge mapping and the mechanism's safety.
buildPriorities.proof: Measure travel and end-stop behavior on the selected reference hardware, then confirm safe travel and edge-to-edge reticle mapping on the bench. Do not treat parts drawings as a verified angle specification.

buildPriorities.title: Keep each player's vibration and solenoid circuit separate
buildPriorities.why: The manual documents independently fused player gun-solenoid power. Preserve the selected hardware's protection and control boundaries rather than inferring a wiring design from the cabinet's appearance.
buildPriorities.proof: A qualified electrical review checks protection and wiring; a controlled two-player test checks that a feedback command intended for one player does not unintentionally actuate the other gun.

releaseNotes.title: This is the 2015 Raw Thrills game, not the 1994 or 1997 Sega games
releaseNotes.body: This guide describes Raw Thrills' 2015 game. Earlier Sega Jurassic Park and The Lost World titles are different games; demonstrating one of them does not demonstrate this release.

releaseNotes.title: Environmental SD and Motion DLX are different cabinets, same game
releaseNotes.body: Raw Thrills sells this software in two cabinets: the 55" Environmental SD sit-down referenced for control detail here, and the 55" Motion DLX, which adds a force-feedback seat — same missions and gun, different furniture.

releaseNotes.title: Primary fire does not use a reload ritual
releaseNotes.body: Two player accounts describe unlimited standard ammunition and no reload. Limited grenades and temporary weapon pickups remain separate resources; a Big Buck Hunter pump gesture does not belong in this control map.
